title: Pedestrian wait times at signalised junctions
asked: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song asked for the median and maximum programmed pedestrian wait times at signalised junctions, whether pedestrians are prioritised in traffic signal timing and whether LTA will consider prioritising them, and whether maximum wait times will be cut to under 60 seconds.
response: The median pedestrian wait at signalised junctions is 120 seconds and the maximum is 140 seconds. Wait times vary with road type, junction size and traffic volume, and Friendly Streets junctions have waits under 60 seconds, with expansion to every town by 2030. Signal timing balances all junction users including buses, and LTA is working on cameras to track pedestrian volume for dynamic adjustment within a range. The green man button's effect depends on the junction.

key_points.point: Median and maximum pedestrian waiting times at signalised junctions are 120 seconds and 140 seconds respectively.
key_points.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
key_points.quote: the median and maximum waiting time for pedestrians at signalised junctions are 120 seconds and 140 seconds respectively

key_points.point: Wait times depend on the nature of the road, junction size and configuration, and prevailing traffic volume.
key_points.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
key_points.quote: Wait times for pedestrians depend on the nature of road, junction size and configuration, as well as prevailing traffic volume.

key_points.point: Waiting times at Friendly Streets signalised junctions are under 60 seconds, and the scheme is being expanded to every town by 2030.
key_points.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
key_points.quote: waiting times at signalised junctions of Friendly Streets, which we are expanding to every town by 2030, are under 60 seconds.

key_points.point: Signal timing must balance all junction users, including vehicles and pedestrians.
key_points.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
key_points.quote: the configuration for signal timing needs to strike a balance among all the users of the junction, whether vehicles on the roads or pedestrians.

key_points.point: Traffic includes public buses that need to stick to a schedule to bring commuters to work on time.
key_points.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
key_points.quote: Traffic is not just private vehicles. It also includes public buses, which need to stick to a schedule to make sure they bring commuters to work on time.

key_points.point: Dynamic systems track traffic volume, and LTA is working on installing cameras at pedestrian waiting areas to track pedestrian volume and adjust traffic light timings dynamically within a range.
key_points.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
key_points.quote: we might want to install cameras at the pedestrian waiting area to track pedestrian volume

key_points.point: The effect of pressing the green man button depends on the junction; at some crossings the lights do not usually change unless someone presses it.
key_points.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
key_points.quote: I think it depends on the junction.

key_points.point: Technology data from the Electronic Road Pricing (ERP) 2.0 system is used to better assess different needs.
key_points.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
key_points.quote: we use technology data from the Electronic Road Pricing (ERP) 2.0 system to allow us to better assess the different needs
